title: Bootstrap Terraform module for KMS/HSM-backed secrets orchestration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reusable, idempotent Terraform module that wires Redwood Private deployments to customer KMS/HSM backends and secrets stores (Vault and AWS Secrets Manager). The module should support: HSM-backed key creation and rotation hooks, Vault transit/kv integration for secret lifecycle, Secrets Manager sync configuration for hybrid customers, encryption-at-rest and envelope encryption patterns, and runbook-friendly health checks that surface misconfigurations. The goal is to give customers a single module to bootstrap secrets infra in a VPC or on-prem environment, and to enable safe, automated upgrades across module versions.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for: kms_provider (aws|gcp|azure|custom-hsm), hsm_config (endpoint, client_cert_ref), vault_address, secrets_manager_sync boolean, key_alias, rotation_period_days, and kms_policy_attachments
Module creates or references a KMS key (or HSM key) without leaking material to state files; private key material must be kept in HSM/KMS only
Module provisions Vault KV/transit roles and policies necessary for Redwood agents to encrypt/decrypt without root tokens
If secrets_manager_sync=true, module configures a one-directional sync from Vault -> AWS Secrets Manager with IAM role, minimal least-privilege policy, and a CloudWatch health metric
Upgrade path documented: v1 -> v2 migration plan where resource renames are avoided or accompanied by migration scripts; tests show zero downtime for live token refresh flows
Health check endpoints + Terraform outputs produce a remediation guide link and a boolean health status for automated checks in the Console
Integration tests exist that run against a local Vault dev server and a mocked HSM (pkcs11 simulator) in CI and pass in the pipeline
Security review completed and PR labeled security-approved before merge
notes: 2025-02-12: RFC drafted — outlined envelope encryption flow and two deployment modes (managed KMS vs. customer HSM). Decision: support both but avoid bundling vendor-specific drivers in module; provide hooks and examples instead.

2025-02-18: Spike completed — validated pkcs11 emulator (SoftHSM) integration and confirmed Terraform provider behavior for importing HSM-backed keys. Found that provider state can contain references to key IDs but not material; flagged for security review.

2025-02-24: Design review with Security and Platform — Security requested default to KMS-only and opt-in for HSM with explicit acceptance. Added input 'hsm_opt_in' and documented additional operator responsibilities.

2025-02-28: Initial implementation pushed to feature branch eng/ENG-23812-kms-bootstrap. Created skeleton module with inputs/outputs and basic Vault policy templates. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1624
2025-03-01: CI integration tests failing intermittently when using Vault dev server due to token TTL. Added retry logic in tests and a step to renew token during long runs.
2025-03-03: Security review kickoff meeting. Action: produce a threat model doc and export for compliance (link below).

Remaining tasks: finalize IAM least-privilege policies, add canary upgrade test to ensure Terraform plan/apply does not rotate keys unexpectedly, author runbook for operator-led HSM firmware/driver upgrades.
implementation_notes: Prefer resource lifecycles and 'prevent_destroy' only for keys that are customer-managed; for Redwood-managed reserved keys allow rotation via Terraform plan when rotation_period_days changes
Keep sensitive outputs empty by default; provide 'example_outputs' variable for demos but do not enable in production
Provide a thin wrapper script to run Vault migration for existing secrets to avoid operator errors during upgrades
Healthchecks: implement Terraform null_resource that registers a monitoring metric (custom CloudWatch metric or a Prometheus pushgateway event) and a README describing failure modes
Acceptance tests should exercise: creation, import of existing key, simulated HSM failover, Vault token TTL expiry and renew, and secrets sync reconciliation
